at overnatte.explanation: "At overnatte" means "to stay overnight", for example at a hotel, a hostel or a friend's house. Vi overnatter på hotel means "We stay the night at a hotel".

sentence.en: We want to stay overnight at a hotel.

en onkel.explanation: "En onkel" means "an uncle". You say min onkel (my uncle), and "onkel Peter" means "Uncle Peter".

sentence.en: My uncle is my father's brother.

en ovn.explanation: "En ovn" means "an oven", the one you bake and roast in. Typical phrases are i ovnen (in the oven) and at tænde ovnen (to turn on the oven). The cooking surface on top is a different word, en kogeplade (a stovetop).

sentence.da: Jeg bager en kage i en varm **ovn**.
sentence.en: I am baking a cake in a hot oven.

et offentligt toilet.explanation: "Et offentligt toilet" means "a public restroom". On signs you may see et herretoilet (a men's toilet) or et dametoilet (a women's toilet).

forms.da: Er der et offentligt toilet her?
forms.en: Is there a public restroom here?

sentence.da: Der er et **offentligt toilet** i parken.
sentence.en: There is a public restroom in the park.

et ord.explanation: "Et ord" means "a word". Hvad betyder det ord? means "What does that word mean?". A dictionary is en ordbog, literally a word book.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke finde det **ord** i ordbogen.
sentence.en: I cannot find that word in the dictionary.

ofte.explanation: "Ofte" means "often". Compare Jeg går ofte i skoven (I often walk in the forest) with Jeg går aldrig i skoven (I never walk in the forest). To ask, say Hvor ofte træner du? (How often do you work out?).

sentence.en: We often eat out.

og.explanation: "Og" means "and": Jeg har en bror og en søster (I have a brother and a sister). Do not mix it up with også (also, too): Jeg kan også lide te (I also like tea). Og sounds like a short o, with no g sound.

sentence.en: I like coffee and tea.

også.explanation: "Også" means "also" or "too". Compare Jeg kommer også (I am coming too) with Jeg kommer heller ikke (I am not coming either). Do not mix it up with og (and): te og kaffe (tea and coffee).

sentence.en: I also want coffee.

okay.explanation: "Okay" means "okay", the same word as in English. You use it to agree or to show you understand.

sentence.en: See you at five. – Okay!

oksekød.explanation: "Oksekød" means "beef". It is made from okse (ox) and kød (meat), so it is literally ox meat. Kød on its own means any kind of meat.

sentence.en: The burger is made of beef.

oktober.explanation: "Oktober" means "October". Danish spells it with a k, where English has a c. Like all month names, it is written with a small letter.

sentence.en: After September comes October.

olie.explanation: "Olie" means "oil". Put the kind in front to name it: rapsolie (rapeseed oil), olivenolie (olive oil).

sentence.en: I fry the meat in oil.

om.explanation: "Om" means "about", in (time from now) or "if". En bog om Danmark means "a book about Denmark". Om en uge means "in a week", unlike i en uge (for a week). And "Jeg ved ikke, om han kommer" means "I do not know if he is coming".

sentence.en: The film starts in an hour.

om aftenen.explanation: "Om aftenen" means "in the evening", for something you do again and again. Compare Jeg læser om aftenen (I read in the evening, every evening) with Jeg læser i aften (I will read this evening, just today).

forms.en: In the evening we watch TV.
What do you do in the evening?

sentence.en: We watch TV in the evening.

om lidt.explanation: "Om lidt" means "in a little while" or "soon". Compare Jeg kommer nu (I am coming now) with Jeg kommer om lidt (I am coming in a little while).

forms.en: I am coming in a little while.
See you in a little while.

sentence.en: The food will be ready in a little while.

om morgenen.explanation: "Om morgenen" means "in the morning", for something you do again and again. Compare Jeg drikker kaffe om morgenen (I drink coffee in the morning, every morning) with Jeg drak kaffe i morges (I drank coffee this morning, just today).

forms.en: I get up in the morning.
In the morning I drink coffee.

sentence.da: Jeg står op klokken seks **om morgenen**.
sentence.en: I get up at six in the morning.

om natten.explanation: "Om natten" means "at night", for something that happens every night. Compare Jeg sover om natten (I sleep at night) with Jeg sov dårligt i nat (I slept badly last night).

sentence.en: Everyone sleeps at night.

om ugen.explanation: "Om ugen" means "per week" or "a week" in how-often answers. Compare tre gange om ugen (three times a week) with to gange om dagen (twice a day) and fem dage om ugen (five days a week).

forms.da: Jeg arbejder fem dage om ugen.
forms.en: I work five days a week.

sentence.en: I work out three times a week.

omkring.explanation: "Omkring" means "around". It works for a place: Vi går omkring søen (We walk around the lake). It also works for a rough number or time: omkring tyve mennesker (about twenty people), omkring klokken otte (around eight o'clock).

sentence.en: There are many trees around the house.

ondt.explanation: "Ondt" means "pain" or "hurt". Danish says Jeg har ondt i maven, literally I have pain in the stomach, where English says my stomach hurts. Do not say Jeg er ondt (I am pain).

sentence.en: My stomach hurts.

onsdag.explanation: "Onsdag" means "Wednesday". Like all day names, it starts with a small letter. Use på onsdag (on Wednesday, coming up) for the next one, and om onsdagen (on Wednesdays) for every week.

sentence.en: After Tuesday comes Wednesday.

op.explanation: "Op" means "up", for moving up. Compare Kom op! (Come up!) with Han er oppe på loftet (He is up in the attic): oppe is for being there. It is also part of at stå op (to get up out of bed).

sentence.en: The cat jumps up onto the table.

oppe.explanation: "Oppe" means "up there", for where something is. Compare Katten hopper op på bordet (The cat jumps up onto the table) with Katten er oppe på bordet (The cat is up on the table). Er du oppe? (Are you up?) asks whether someone is out of bed.

sentence.en: The book is up on the shelf.

optaget.explanation: "Optaget" means "busy", taken or "occupied". Use it for a phone line, a toilet, a seat, or a person who has no time. Er her optaget? (Is this taken?) asks whether a seat is taken.

sentence.en: The toilet is occupied right now.

orange.explanation: "Orange" means "orange", the colour. For the fruit, Danes say en appelsin (an orange), not orange. The colour word never changes, whatever it describes: en orange bil (an orange car), orange biler (orange cars).

sentence.en: Carrots are orange.

os.explanation: "Os" means "us". Compare Vi ser ham (We see him) with Han ser os (He sees us): vi is we, os is us. It is also used after words like med (with): Kom med os! (Come with us!).

related.en: you (more than one, after words like "med")

sentence.en: Do you want to come with us?

ost.explanation: "Ost" means "cheese". When you mean one kind of cheese, say en ost: en fransk ost means "a French cheese". Without en it is cheese in general.

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **ost** på brød.
sentence.en: I like cheese on bread.

otte.explanation: "Otte" means "eight". Do not mix it up with atten (eighteen): otte børn (eight children) but atten børn (eighteen children).

sentence.en: After seven comes eight.

ottende.explanation: "Ottende" means "eighth": den ottende dag (the eighth day). It is also used for dates: den ottende marts (the eighth of March).

sentence.da: Efter den syvende dag kommer den **ottende** dag.
sentence.en: After the seventh day comes the eighth day.

ovenpå.explanation: "Ovenpå" means "upstairs". It works for where something is and for going there: Jeg bor ovenpå (I live upstairs), Jeg går ovenpå (I go upstairs). Compare Soveværelset er ovenpå (The bedroom is upstairs) with Køkkenet er nedenunder (The kitchen is downstairs).

sentence.en: We sleep upstairs in the house.

over.explanation: "Over" means "over", above or "across". Compare Lampen hænger over bordet (The lamp hangs above the table) with Han går over gaden (He walks across the street). With amounts it means "more than": over to timer (more than two hours).

sentence.en: The lamp hangs over the table.

overalt.explanation: "Overalt" means "everywhere". Compare Jeg leder overalt (I look everywhere) with Den er ingen steder (It is nowhere). It can also start a sentence: Overalt er der blomster (Everywhere there are flowers).

sentence.en: I look everywhere for the key.

overskyet.explanation: "Overskyet" means "overcast", with the whole sky covered by cloud. It is stronger than skyet (cloudy), which can mean only some clouds.

sentence.en: The sky is overcast today.
